steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: This is your last warning, Tonya.

steps.name: Soldier
steps.text: You'll be dealt with harshly, if you're caught spreading rumors and inciting panic again. You'd better stay on the straight and narrow!

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Doing it by day doesn't work. I'll have to...

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: Are you alright, Tonya?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Mark? Were you waiting for me?

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: We all saw the way the soldier grabbed you downstairs. Did they throw you in jail again?

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: You shouldn't do this... think of your family.

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: All those things you keep talking about every day, there's no proof at all.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: Yeah. More importantly, are you hurt? I just came back from the clinic. We'll have to go back if you're injured.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I'm fine. Were you at the clinic, Mark? What did Nadezhda say? Is my sister getting better?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: Her condition's holding stable right now. No need to be too worried.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: It was my fault for bringing back the work jacket to wash at home. How could I—

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: Let the government folks worry about any strange illnesses. We just take care of ourselves.

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: We'll have a barbecue and celebrate once your sister gets better!

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: Great! I just made sausages!

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: Finally! I haven't had them in ages. I started to miss them my second day here—

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: But I haven't found Kirill yet...

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: See? This is all good stuff. I just cut a couple, and my hands are already all greasy.

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: They'll taste so good cooked in soup. My mouth's already watering...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Guys! I haven't seen Kirill for days, and no one answers when I knock on his door. None of you have seen him either, have you?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: This is no joke! This is no time to relax.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: ...Didn't we already tell you, Tonya?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: You're pushing yourself too hard.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: Did you forget that Kirill just lost his wife and kid? I guess staying in this place brings back bad memories.

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: Maybe he left Zelgrad and went home.

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: It's unusual that he didn't say goodbye to us, but you can't just assume he's missing, or that it has anything to do with your sister's illness...

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: Surely the police will come if something's not right.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Are we just going to pretend that nothing's happening? You saw the strange spots and bruises on Nina—

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: And that's all there is, a little bit of rash. Happens all the time in this environment and weather. A little bit of rest is all it takes.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: You said it's the clothes of those white coats, but I've been washing the same clothes, and there's nothing wrong with me.
With a smile, he puts a hand on Tonya's shoulder. Faint green spots are visible underneath the tiny hairs.
Tonya jumps, causing the others to look at each other in confusion as she struggles to explain her actions.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: ...Tonya?

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: Well, she's under a lot of stress.

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: Look, Tonya, I know you have our best interests in your hearts, but it's best if you don't talk about those strange things anymore.

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: We're so happy here. Living in Zelgrad is like springtime compared to life elsewhere in Ursus. We should cherish it.

steps.name: Concerned Resident
steps.text: We'll go and see Nina tomorrow, then pick up the other kids from school. Have a good meal, drink to your heart's content, and forget all those things, alright?

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: That's right, Tonya.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Resident
steps.text: Things will get better.
Night falls, and a stiff silence comes upon the city.
A dark shadow vaults over the wall, arriving at an abandoned warehouse, avoiding the things scattered on the ground on tiptoes.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: ...Good, the stuff's all here.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I can't wait. Tomorrow has to be the day—
The day for what?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: —Who's there?!

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: ...Who are you... ugh—

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Quiet, unless you want your arm broken.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: W-Who are you? What do you know?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: Y-You're interfering with the Reunion! My comrades will have your head!

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Enough bluffing. I've been following you, and I can tell that you and your 'comrades' have nothing to do with the Reunion.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Five bottles of flammable liquid, a bundle of Originium explosives... the Reunion isn't dumb enough to attack a gate guarded by the First Army with just this.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: ...I didn't think it would defeat them. But what they're doing behind those walls must have something to do with the strange events that have been happening lately.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: So you want to blow a hole in the wall, set a fire, get people's attention.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You think the things the Army's hiding in the labs will come to light if you make enough of a commotion.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: But these cans and bottles are all the preparation you've made...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You haven't even investigated what that wall's made of.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: A wall is a wall! Stone or steel, what else could it be? If it could be made, it could be destroyed.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You think you can set the explosives under the patrols' noses, when I managed to pin you to the ground by myself?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I practiced! I'm prepared!

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Did you practice on location? You think you can deploy and detonate it at a range that they won't find out?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: You don't understand! You never saw—you don't know that all of Zelgrad is now in danger from some unknown source. I need to get people's attention, even if—

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You still don't understand?

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You're facing the First Army. Fighting them by yourself is futile.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Your 'comrades' are just ordinary people whose eyes aren't open yet. No one is truly on your side.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Besides, how can you be sure that the incidents have something to do with the experiments behind the wall? You know the experiments exist, but you have no inkling about the details...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: How do you intend to explain to the people once you've gotten their attention?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: ...At least, I have to make them look up...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You want them to look. How about we look at the present? Forget your neighbors. Do your closest family fully believe what you're saying?

steps.name: Sobbing Girl
steps.text: Will you come and pick me up today, Tonya?

steps.name: Sobbing Girl
steps.text: I don't want to stay at Uncle Mark's house anymore. It's not our home, and I don't want to bother them...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: ...I'll take you out to picnic once spring comes and Nina has gotten better, alright?

steps.name: Sobbing Girl
steps.text: Has Nina gotten better? You've been so busy, we hardly see you other than bedtime.

steps.name: Sobbing Girl
steps.text: It's like you're not around even when you're at home. We have to call your name several times to get you to answer. You're not at the table or in bed—

steps.name: Sobbing Girl
steps.text: You don't hug us any more. Why?

steps.name: Sobbing Girl
steps.text: What are you doing, Tonya...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: But what else can I do? I...

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: I tried everything I could think of. Nina's still in the clinic. That strange bruising might have spread already. I don't even dare go and see her—

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: What can I do...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Calmed down a little?

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: You... you sound like you know Reunion well.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: That's not important.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You want to know what you can do? There's always one thing, and only one thing—

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Find more evidence.

steps.name: Tonya
steps.text: More evidence...

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: You need more evidence to prove that your sister's condition is not an isolated incident, and that it could affect everyone.

steps.name: Crownslayer
steps.text: Convince them that this is a matter of life and death to them. Only then would they listen to you.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Let go, Valiya.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: (Whisper) There's a soldier with them.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Thank you...

steps.name: Serious Soldier
steps.text: What—

steps.name: Serious Soldier
steps.text: Oh, I forgot, somebody has moved into the second floor.

steps.name: Serious Soldier
steps.text: Follow me.

steps.name: Red
steps.text: Did you also arrive in Zelgrad today?

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: We—

steps.name: Serious Soldier
steps.text: That's enough chit-chat.

steps.name: Serious Soldier
steps.text: You'll be working in the same district, there's plenty of time for you to talk then. Let's go.

steps.name: Serious Soldier
steps.text: Who's coming with me to registration?

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Excuse me, I have a question... if there are other people on the second floor, while the first floor is the security room and public spaces, where do the rest of us stay?

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: There are three of us who are not yet housed.

steps.name: Serious Soldier
steps.text: Can't you squeeze in? Or I could take them to another building.

steps.name: Serious Soldier
steps.text: But maybe there'll be room here in a few days...

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: (In a few days...?)

steps.name: Serious Soldier
steps.text: What's your plan?
The youth exchanges a glance with the miner and shakes head at the soldier.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: We'll find a way to squeeze in.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: 'Has it lathered up yet?'
'The blade's still hot.'

steps.name: Tardy Worker
steps.text: Excuse me... excuse me.

steps.name: Tardy Worker
steps.text: Sorry, those guys were a pain! Team A should be all present now.

steps.name: Tardy Worker
steps.text: Captain Pavel!
The man gives the miner at the front a crooked salute.

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Good work, lads.

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: We had been operating according to the original plan, but we realized we had lost contact with your group after we found a good gathering spot. If you didn't find a way to reestablish communication...

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Good thing we had the contingency. What's the current situation here?

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: This location is temporary. The residential layer is connected to the apartments and some districts. Land is at a premium in the satellite city, and this place isn't likely to remain abandoned for long based on the frequency of patrols.

steps.name: Pavel
steps.text: We can't stay too long. I have an idea what you're trying to do and I support you, but you should explain it to the others. We'll get this done quickly.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Everybody, listen up.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Our primary objective is to ascertain what's going on here, then try to find the Infected who came before us but seem to have gone off the grid.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Something's clearly off about this place. There is surveillance everywhere. Things are even harder than the last time we entered a nomadic city.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: We still need a few more days to plot the patrol routes, but we already understand that the Infected in the satellite city are separately housed.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: That's the question that I want to discuss—we've passed through many towns and villages, but never before have we seen soldiers patrolling the streets and residences with such frequency.

steps.name: Perplexed Miner
steps.text: There were more guards around our apartments than there were on the streets along the way. That alone is suspicious enough.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Right, that's why I decided to test them while there was still daylight.

steps.name: Nervous Guard
steps.text: This is your last warning! Not one step further!

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Sorry, sir, I didn't mean to—

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: we just did a head count, and some people were missing. We were concerned that they might get into trouble wandering around the city.

steps.name: Nervous Guard
steps.text: You can't go through here! Give me their names and descriptions, and the Army will find them.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Wait... I think that's—

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Karl! Is that you, Karl?
The soldier instinctively looks in the direction in which the youth is calling. The seemingly frail figure quickly slips underneath his arm and gets through.

steps.name: Nervous Guard
steps.text: Blyat! I need backup! Get that one!

spans.text: I need backup! Get that one!

steps.text: More shouting and the rattling of boots, and the youth is quickly surrounded by a circle of black military uniforms.
Several hands reach out to grab those thin arms, but none of the soldiers pull their weapons, despite their fierce expressions.

steps.name: Anxious Miner
steps.text: That's dangerous! You should tell us before taking such risks.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Thank you, but the reason I dared to try was that I noticed that the soldiers weren't equipped with lethal weapons.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: And I was right. They seem unwilling to harm me for some reason.

steps.name: Perplexed Miner
steps.text: You mean they want to keep an eye on us, but not hurt us?

steps.name: Perplexed Miner
steps.text: Sounds like a glorified prison.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Worse. We have soldiers instead of prison guards, and we know nothing about what the Army's intentions are.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Perhaps this intention is the reason why they've suddenly opened their doors to the Infected.

steps.name: Perplexed Miner
steps.text: Uh—

steps.name: Hesitant Miner
steps.text: ...I've been talking to the local Infected all afternoon.

steps.name: Hesitant Miner
steps.text: They said most of the Infected are under the care of the Army and housed in designated apartments.

steps.name: Hesitant Miner
steps.text: Prior to that, however, they were sent to a local clinic, where the doctors don't care whether you're Infected, and accept the factory scrips that only circulate in the industrial districts.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: You mean those paper-thin metal plates that are only seen in this place?

steps.name: Hesitant Miner
steps.text: Yes, some of us who came in earlier got it yesterday. Strangely enough, wages here are issued daily...

steps.name: Hesitant Miner
steps.text: Anyway, after Zelgrad's recent Infected policies were introduced, everyone assumes that clinic is working with the Army.

steps.name: Hesitant Miner
steps.text: Maybe collecting data for them for Oripathy research? If the Army's really holding us like prisoners, then this so-called clinic...

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: ...I see. Good work.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: The clinic sounds suspicious. We should investigate.

steps.name: Calm Youth
steps.text: Go back and prepare, wait for my word. Be discreet when moving weapons.

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: Alright!

options: We'll talk once the room is secure.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No problems. The room's clean, no surveillance or recording equipment.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I put jammers by the wall, just in case. It's one-time, but it'll be useful until they find out.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The soldiers said the Marshal of the First Army is treating Rhodes Island like VIPs, arranging the best accommodations and heavy security...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: In other words, we're being watched.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: So the soldiers outside the hotel...

options: Probably here to keep an eye on us.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Yeah, everything feels so eerie here.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Like that woman who stopped us at the transfer area earlier today!

options: She was talking about 'dust never seen before that infects people'.
But there are already a lot of Infected living here.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Unless... she wasn't talking about Originium dust or Oripathy.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If there's another illness that we're not aware of...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Could it be a new symptom of Oripathy? I remember that Raidian raised a hypothesis in her report about why news of Infected mutation first spread from the Far North.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Even though we know now that it was likely a ruse by the Grand Duchess, wouldn't those involved have come to the conclusion of Oripathy mutations too?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: As was the case the last time, we can't jump to a conclusion until we learn more.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: I tried asking questions during the day, but the locals don't want to talk.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Or rather, they're quite happy to talk, but as soon as you ask whether there has been anything unusual going on, they either ignore the question, or fall silent altogether.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The officer who led the way was the same. He reminded me not to have too much contact with the locals.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Was it for our own safety, or something else?

options: Remember the buildings hidden behind the wall?
What the Army is trying to hide is probably in the buildings behind the wall.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: The locals don't know what's behind the wall either. It's like an entirely different city to them.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: It's strange. It seems like the First Army's research doesn't rely on the Infected here for labor—why do they do this, then?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The open areas of Zelgrad are no different from the average nomadic city. The First Army's research institute must lie behind the wall.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Based on the officer's reaction, the letter of safe passage from Chairman Witte isn't enough to get us through that wall.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: And we've heard nothing from the Marshal who was supposed to welcome us.

options: Grypherburg has no reason to deceive us.
Grypherburg doesn't control the First Army.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: Is that so? I didn't quite feel it.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I noticed too... this sort of weather is not normal.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, do you remember about the mysterious new bomb that Hellagur mentioned?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It might have something to do with the Sarcophagus... we need more information, and quickly.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: We've got just the right woman for the job—you up for it, Raidian?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Yes, I should be able to intercept some of the communications.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: The code the USSG obtained which Dur-nar sent us is used by large military installations. These facilities often send electrical signals at a specific frequency.

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: What do you think, Doctor?

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Here we go—
The crack of static electricity echoes through the empty room.
Everyone present has seen Raidian's Arts many times, but they cannot help but hold their breath, watching her furrowed brows and twitching lips.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Whisper) Raidian, are you really gonna be okay?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: (Whisper) Trust her, she's master—

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Ugh—argh!
Raidian barely took a step before stumbling and falling.

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: Raidian—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Overload! I brought emergency meds. Hang in there, Raidian!

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Raidian
steps.text: Electric-magnetic radiation... here...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Raidian!
The night is deathly silent, except for the echoing of orderly footsteps in the distance, magnified by the emptiness.
There was food and clean water in the break room by the sentry post prior to the shift change in the patrols in this district, a perk that other units do not enjoy.

Ever since the Generalik returned to Zelgrad, they occasionally got off an hour or two early, and extra supplies began appearing in the break room, which they were even allowed to bring home to their families.
No one knew why. No one asked, because why would they mess with a good thing while it lasts?
Nor did anyone suspect that the foodstuff had been tampered with. Tonight, someone has made sure that they would not leave the break room for a while after their usual little feast.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: (Their replacements should appear in four minutes, based on the patrol routes.)

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: (Even if Anatoliy doesn't show up personally, his bodyguards should be here to 'act in his capacity'.)

steps.name: Panicked Soldier
steps.text: Mmph—mmph!

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Have you thought it over? You can talk if you have, or you can join your comrades on the floor.

steps.name: Panicked Soldier
steps.text: (Nods frantically)

steps.name: Panicked Soldier
steps.text: Hff... ha—

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Was it the Generalik's unit who replaced you today?

steps.name: Panicked Soldier
steps.text: I-I've never seen them, I don't know—

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: (Raises hand)

steps.name: Panicked Soldier
steps.text: We don't know who takes over the shifts! We get notified to stop at the sentry post, and that someone will take over the next shift, but no one tells us who's taking over.

steps.name: Panicked Soldier
steps.text: Although, it will certainly make sense if it was the Generalik...

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: What if it isn't?

steps.name: Panicked Soldier
steps.text: Then there should be another unit on patrol, but everyone's schedule is packed, and no one can be in two places at the same time.

steps.name: Panicked Soldier
steps.text: Unless there's a unit that's not on the shift schedule—the Generalik's bodyguards.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Panicked Soldier
steps.text: It could only be his bodyguards. If he doesn't show up personally, his bodyguards would be patrolling on his behalf.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: (Quietly) He's here.

steps.name: Young Voice
steps.text: ...How's the fuel?

steps.name: Low Voice
steps.text: As you commanded.

steps.name: Young Voice
steps.text: Is there enough?

steps.name: Low Voice
steps.text: There have not been any reports about shortages.

steps.name: Young Voice
steps.text: Keep an eye on them. Our people need to be involved in every step. There must be no mistake...

steps.name: Young Voice
steps.text: You should understand.
The source of the young voice appears in Sirka's field of vision.
She has never seen the Generalik before, but she is certain that she has found him.
The tyrant of Zelgrad, the only son of the First Army's marshal...

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: (Softly) Anatoliy Svetlanov Buterin.
Gazing upon the malicious visage illuminated by the flickering searchlight, so reminiscent of the Marshal's younger days, Sirka clutches her dagger and hides herself in the darkness.

The guards around her mark do not matter. The unfamiliar girl next to him does not matter. All that matters is the spot that her blade needs to find, the neck, the heart, or one of the arteries, where a single well-placed stab will kill—
She is ready, as she has been so many times before. But she did not expect the prey to detect her.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: —Who's there?!

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Anatoliy—
But Originium Arts have set up the perfect environment for the assassin, and the prey's awareness cannot stop the killer's blade.
A sudden breeze rustles clothes and masks the approaching footsteps, the leap, and the sound of dagger ripping through air—

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: Sorry, Generalik.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: I need to 'borrow' your life.
The bodyguards have detected the intruder, even without hearing her sound.
But the weapon has already pierced the target's neck, and withdrawn as slickly as it went in.
Sirka is not in a hurry to escape. Without a pause, she proceeds to make her next stab, only to realize that there is no blood flowing from the first wound.

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: What—
It seems she has simply cut a gap in some kind of hard, golden substance.
It does not even look human.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Ugh...

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: What... is this?

steps.name: Sirka
steps.text: How could this be? I had—

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: There's the assassin! Get her!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: After her... hurry—

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: After her!!

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: After her! Don't let her get away!

steps.name: Excited Soldier
steps.text: You two, stay here and protect the Generalik and Hierda! The rest of you, with me!

steps.name: Composed Soldier
steps.text: Generalik, your injury—

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...Let me.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Let me see his wound...
The girl lays her hands on the young man's neck.
There was a piece of Originium crystal hidden underneath the collar, which should have been ripped open along with the flesh around it to reveal the bone beneath.
Underneath her palms, however, the injury is less serious than first imagined.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...It seems the Originium has already begun to repair the wound. There's no need to worry.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What did you say?

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I said, it seems the Originium is repairing your wound. Are you in pain?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I don't feel anything. But that suka pierced my neck—

spans.text: I don't feel anything. But that

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I felt it!

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I couldn't speak, couldn't make a sound... I felt like I had died.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: Maybe she only cut the Originium crystal on the surface of your body. I'm sorry I wasn't able to stop the assassin...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Hah, what can you do? A sword would go right through you without even slowing down.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Maybe she did kill me. Maybe I would be a corpse, if not for you—your miracle.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: I can tell the difference between having my skin cut and having the artery in my neck cut.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: It's not a miracle... *sigh*.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: What I want to know is, what does this mean? Does it mean I can't die? Not even after a thousand assassination attempts?

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: And it's all because of you, even though you claim you can't save me, that you only remove my pain...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: You're the real deal, my friend. You've saved me twice now...

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Argh...
The young man's voice grows weaker after his initial excitement. The repairing of his wound has drained him.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: You need to rest.

steps.name: Anatoliy
steps.text: Tell me, how can I repay...?
He soon falls unconscious.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: ...I don't need repayment, Anatoliy.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: I never have...
Hierda looks up in the direction where the assassin escaped, soldiers in hot pursuit.
She recalls those eyes that she saw in the darkness, bright and calm.
Desperate and dangerous.

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: She was Infected too...

steps.name: Hierda
steps.text: How did it come to this? Is there anything I can do?
